Hi Evan / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side after the demo & data walk-through. Attachments: velori_eval_results_q1.csv (sample evals), prompt_set_v1.txt (seed prompts), MAP_draft_VeloriHealth.pdf (initial mutual action plan).

Call highlights / observations:
- Primary task: clinical note summarization + structured extraction for downstream analytics. Key success metrics are QA accuracy on slot extraction, ROUGE-L for summarization, and precision on PHI redaction.
- Baseline: VeloriBaseline-1 (your current in-house model) — sample evals attached. Baseline QA EM: 78.4%, ROUGE-L: 0.62, PHI redaction precision: 99.1%.
- Candidate open models we discussed: Llama2-13B (8-bit), Mistral-7B/Mistral-Instruct variants, RedOpen-6. Tradeoffs: cost, latency, and willingness to quantize.

Recommended short pilot approach (3 weeks):
1) Evaluate 2 open-model variants in parallel vs your baseline on the same prompt set: Mistral-Instruct-8B-quant (fast/cheap) and Llama2-13B-8q.
2) Acceptance thresholds for parity: 
   - QA (slot extraction) absolute delta <= 2.5% (EM) vs baseline
   - ROUGE-L within 3 points absolute
   - No more than 1% regression on PHI redaction precision; any drop triggers manual review
3) Run end-to-end evals on your 2k holdout cases (we've run a 200-case quick pass attached).
4) Ops config suggestions: target p50 latency <= 220ms for interactive flows; batch endpoints for nightly bulk.

Next steps we propose from Redwood side:
- Deliver a pilot config and run full 2k eval within 5 business days once you share the holdout set (we can accept S3 link or upload to the shared Drive).
- Recommend Mistral-Instruct-8B-quant as the initial candidate for throughput-first testing; Llama2-13B for quality-first testing.
- Draft a short Mutual Action Plan (attached) and proposed dates for a mid-pilot check on week 2.

Questions for you (action items):
- Can you confirm the S3 path for the 2k holdout?
- Any additional redaction constraints (regions/types) besides PHI?
- Who should receive access to the evaluation Drive folder?

Thanks — I’ll loop Dev & Jasmine on the config details below so we can get an initial benchmark spun up.

Hi all — quick technical notes and configuration suggestions to make the pilot deterministic and comparable to your baseline.

Recommended model picks (first pass):
- Llama2-13B-8q (quality arm) — inference with dynamic KV cache, temp 0.0 for extraction tasks, top_p 0.95 for summarization subtask.
- Mistral-Instruct-8B-quant (cost/throughput arm) — temp 0.0, top_k=40, aggressive prompt pruning to reduce token counts.

Evaluation harness details (so results match):
- Use identical prompt_set_v1.txt for both models (attached). Do not apply additional system-level rewrites; replicate the same preprocessing pipeline (token normalization + date canonicalization).
- Metrics: QA EM and F1 (slot extraction), ROUGE-L for summary, per-case latency (p50/p95), and a binary hallucination flag. We'll produce both absolute and relative deltas vs VeloriBaseline-1.
- Safety check: run a regex-based PHI redaction validator post-output (we can provide our validator). Any hallucination or introduced identifiers -> fail-case.

Operational knobs for Redwood Dedicated/Hosted testing:
- Suggest autoscale ceiling at 8 shards for the quality arm to keep p95 latency < 450ms during parallel runs.
- Enable prefix KV caching for repeated patient-context flows; this reduces token CPU by ~12% in our tests.

Expectations and timeline:
- If we get the S3 holdout by EOD Thu, Redwood will: spin both models, run the 2k eval, and deliver a full report + diff deck within 5 business days.
- Cost estimate: preliminary expected per-1000-summary token cost (hosted) for Llama2-13B: ~$14; Mistral-8B-quant: ~$5 (numbers are illustrative and will vary based on seq length / batching).

Attaching MAP_draft_VeloriHealth.pdf — Neha, please push any commercial cadence/contract notes into the MAP where relevant.
